name: 403. Deepgram provider: Nova-3 transcription by file or URL, options as query parameters, duration usage (deepgram provider) [SERIAL]
description: TXE-6434 (Bifrost-Tokun contract C3, C4, C5, C6, C12): the deepgram provider serves POST /v1/audio/transcriptions on Deepgram's pre-recorded API, POST /v1/listen. Rows 403.1 to 403.8 run against the provider error fixture, which stands in for api.deepgram.com and keeps every call it receives, so they pin what reaches the vendor and how often: with x-bf-api-key one request is exactly one upstream call under the named key, for a transcript and for a vendor error alike (two keys are configured; the other is never tried); the options the caller sends as form fields arrive as query parameters under their own names, a repeated field once per value; a file arrives as the request body, and a url with no file arrives as the JSON body {"url": ...} that Deepgram fetches itself; usage is {type: duration, seconds: metadata.duration x metadata.channels}, 61 for a 30.5 second two-channel call; raw_response carries metadata.request_id; a vendor 402 keeps its status, code and text and is provider_billing; a 200 without results is 502 provider_empty_result; a field Deepgram cannot take (response_format srt, callback) is 400 caller_unsupported_parameter and makes no upstream call. They are skipped unless providerErrorFixture=1. Row 403.9 is the live row: one Nova-3 transcription by URL, skipped while DEEPGRAM_API_KEY is unset; it also passes against the fixture. Rows 403.10 and 403.11 are the async route, against the fixture: POST /v1/async/audio/transcriptions accepts a url-only Deepgram job, and GET /v1/async/audio/transcriptions/{job_id} returns it completed with the transcript and the duration usage, after exactly one upstream call carrying the JSON url body.

item.name: 403.1 /v1/audio/transcriptions - a file with a named key is one upstream call, options arrive as query parameters - deepgram/nova-3 (deepgram provider)

exec: pm.test('deepgram setup: the fixture was reset', function () {
// wire: the calls that reached the Deepgram stand-in, in order.

function wire(cb) { pm.sendRequest({ url: FX + '/__wire', method: 'GET' }, function (err, res) { pm.test('the fixture answered /__wire', function () { pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null); }); cb(res.json().data[0].calls.filter(function (c) { return c.path === '/v1/listen'; })); }); }
// params: a call's query string as name -> list of values, in the order sent.

function params(call) { var out = {}; call.query.replace(/^\?/, '').split('&').forEach(function (pair) { if (!pair) { return; } var i = pair.indexOf('='); var k = decodeURIComponent(pair.slice(0, i).replace(/\+/g, ' ')); var v = decodeURIComponent(pair.slice(i + 1).replace(/\+/g, ' ')); (out[k] = out[k] || []).push(v); }); return out; }
pm.test('the transcript and the billable duration come back', function () {
pm.expect(j.text, pm.response.text()).to.eql("Yeah. As as much as, it's worth celebrating, the first, spacewalk.");
pm.test('exactly one upstream call, under the named key, with the audio as the body', function () {
